description: M2 smoke test: 10 paraphrased questions over the RAG vs long-context corpus. A question is a hit if a top-k result comes from the expected paper on one of the listed pages. Pages were found by locating each fact in the corpus; questions avoid copying the papers' wording. M3 replaces this with a 30-40 question benchmark labelled at passage level.

questions.question: Does where the answer sits inside a long prompt change how accurately a model responds?
How can a system choose, for each query, between retrieval and reading the full context, in order to save cost?
Does keeping retrieved chunks in the order they appear in the original document improve RAG answers?
Can a model with a short context window plus retrieval match a model whose context window was extended?
What changes if the retriever works with large units of several thousand tokens instead of short paragraphs?
Why can giving a long-context model more retrieved passages make its answers worse?
Do synthetic needle-in-a-haystack tests predict how well a model handles real long-context tasks?
Which kinds of reasoning do long-context models still struggle with when replacing databases and SQL?
Beyond what context length do most models stop giving consistently accurate answers in RAG?
How much extra does it cost to put the whole document collection in the prompt instead of retrieving a few passages?
